rows.stem: If mode and median of given set of observations are 13 and 11 respectively, then the value of mean is :
rows.solution:
Use the empirical relation \(\text{Mode} = 3\,\text{Median} - 2\,\text{Mean}\).

\(13 = 3(11) - 2\,\text{Mean}\), so \(2\,\text{Mean} = 33 - 13 = 20\) and \(\text{Mean} = 10\). This is option (C) \(10\).

rows.stem: In the adjoining figure, AC is diameter of larger circle with centre O. AB is tangent to smaller circle with centre O. If OD = r, then BC is equal to :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - D (the point where AB touches the smaller circle, with OD drawn) and B (where the tangent meets the larger circle, joined to C) are named only in the drawing of the two concentric circles. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
AB touches the smaller circle at D, so the radius \(OD \perp AB\). AB is also a chord of the larger circle, and the perpendicular from the centre bisects it, so D is the mid-point of AB.

AC is a diameter of the larger circle, so O is the mid-point of AC.

In triangle ABC, the segment OD joins the mid-points of AC and AB, so by the mid-point theorem \(OD \parallel BC\) and \(OD = \dfrac{1}{2}BC\). So \(BC = 2\,OD = 2r\).

This is option (C) \(2r\).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem: Letters A to F are mentioned on six faces of a die such that each face has a different letter. Two such dice are thrown simultaneously. The probability that vowels turn up on both the dice is :
rows.solution:
Two dice give \(6 \times 6 = 36\) equally likely outcomes. The vowels among A to F are A and E, so each die shows a vowel on 2 faces, and both show vowels in \(2 \times 2 = 4\) outcomes.

\(P(\text{vowels on both}) = \dfrac{4}{36} = \dfrac{1}{9}\), which is option (C) \(\dfrac{1}{9}\).

rows.stem: The distance of point \(P(1, -1)\) from x-axis is :
rows.solution:
The distance of a point from the x-axis is the absolute value of its y-coordinate.

For \(P(1, -1)\) it is \(|-1| = 1\). (A distance cannot be negative, so \(-1\) is not possible.)

This is option (A) \(1\).

\(\sec A = 2\cos A\) means \(\dfrac{1}{\cos A} = 2\cos A\), so \(\cos^2 A = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(\cos A = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).

So \(A = 45^\circ\). Check: \(\sec 45^\circ = \sqrt{2}\) and \(2\cos 45^\circ = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\).

This is option (C) \(45^\circ\).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Unit digit of \(3^n\) cannot be an even number for any natural number n.

**Reason (R) :** 2 is not a prime factor of \(3^n\) for any natural number n.
rows.context: In question number 19 and 20, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct option :

options.label: A
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The unit digits of \(3^1, 3^2, 3^3, 3^4, \ldots\) are 3, 9, 7, 1 and then repeat, so the unit digit of \(3^n\) is never even. The Assertion is true.

\(3^n = 3 \times 3 \times \cdots \times 3\), and by the uniqueness of prime factorisation its only prime factor is 3. So 2 is not a prime factor of \(3^n\). The Reason is true.

A number ends in an even digit exactly when it is divisible by 2. Since 2 does not divide \(3^n\), its unit digit cannot be even, so the Reason explains the Assertion. This is option (A).

rows.stem:
Renu and Simran were born in the year 2000 which is a leap year. Find the probability that :

(i) both have same birthday.

(ii) both have different birthdays.
rows.solution:
2000 is a leap year, so it has 366 days, and each of the 366 dates is taken as equally likely for each birthday.

(i) Whatever Renu's birthday, Simran's falls on the same day in 1 of the 366 cases: \(P(\text{same birthday}) = \dfrac{1}{366}\).

(ii) \(P(\text{different birthdays}) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{366} = \dfrac{365}{366}\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem:
Solve the following system of equations algebraically :

\(73x - 37y = 109\)

\(37x - 73y = 1\)
rows.solution:
The coefficients are swapped between the equations, so add and subtract them.

Subtracting the second from the first: \(36x + 36y = 108\), so \(x + y = 3\) ... (1)

Adding: \(110x - 110y = 110\), so \(x - y = 1\) ... (2)

Adding (1) and (2): \(2x = 4\), so \(x = 2\), and then \(y = 1\).

Check: \(73(2) - 37(1) = 109\) and \(37(2) - 73(1) = 1\).

\(x = 2\), \(y = 1\).

rows.subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
rows.stem: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the zeroes of the polynomial \(ax^2 - x + c\). Obtain a polynomial whose zeroes are \(\alpha - 3\) and \(\beta - 3\).
rows.solution:
For \(ax^2 - x + c\): \(\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{1}{a}\) and \(\alpha\beta = \dfrac{c}{a}\).

Sum of the new zeroes: \((\alpha - 3) + (\beta - 3) = \alpha + \beta - 6 = \dfrac{1}{a} - 6 = \dfrac{1 - 6a}{a}\).

Product: \((\alpha - 3)(\beta - 3) = \alpha\beta - 3(\alpha + \beta) + 9 = \dfrac{c}{a} - \dfrac{3}{a} + 9 = \dfrac{c - 3 + 9a}{a}\).

The polynomial is \(x^2 - \left(\dfrac{1 - 6a}{a}\right)x + \dfrac{c - 3 + 9a}{a}\), or, multiplying by \(a\),

\(ax^2 - (1 - 6a)x + (c - 3 + 9a)\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is 70 cm. The length of the rectangle is 5 cm more than twice is breadth. Express the given situation as a system of linear equations in two variables and hence solve it.
rows.solution:
Let the length be \(x\) cm and the breadth \(y\) cm.

The perimeter is 70 cm, so \(2(x + y) = 70\), that is

\(x + y = 35\) ... (1)

The length is 5 cm more than twice the breadth, so \(x = 2y + 5\), that is

\(x - 2y = 5\) ... (2)

Substituting \(x = 2y + 5\) in (1): \(3y + 5 = 35\), so \(y = 10\), and then \(x = 2(10) + 5 = 25\).

The length is 25 cm and the breadth is 10 cm.

rows.subtopic: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem:
A bat manufacturing company made a huge bat for charity and got it signed by world cup winning team.

The dimensions of the bat which is in the form of a cuboid with a cylindrical handle at the top are as follows :

length = 2 m, width = 0.5 m, thickness = 0.1 m

diameter of cylindrical part = 0.1 m

height of cylindrical part = 0.7 m

Find the volume of wood used in the bat. Also, find the total surface area of the wooden bat.
rows.solution:
The radius of the cylindrical handle is \(\dfrac{0.1}{2} = 0.05\) m, that is \(\dfrac{1}{20}\) m.

Volume of wood \(=\) volume of cuboid \(+\) volume of cylinder

\(= 2 \times 0.5 \times 0.1 + \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{1}{20} \times \dfrac{1}{20} \times 0.7 = 0.1 + 0.0055 = 0.1055\) m\(^3\) (that is, \(\dfrac{211}{2000}\) m\(^3\)).

For the surface, the handle's base covers a circle of radius 0.05 m on the top face of the cuboid, and the handle's own top end is a circle of the same size. One removes that area and the other adds it back, so

total surface area \(=\) TSA of cuboid \(+\) curved surface area of cylinder

\(= 2(2 \times 0.5 + 0.5 \times 0.1 + 0.1 \times 2) + 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{1}{20} \times 0.7\)

\(= 2(1.25) + 0.22 = 2.72\) m\(^2\) (that is, \(\dfrac{68}{25}\) m\(^2\)).

rows.stem:
Following table shows the absentees record of 40 students in an academic year :

| **Number of Days** | **Number of Students** |
|---|---|
| 2-6 | 11 |
| 6-10 | 10 |
| 10-14 | 7 |
| 14-18 | 4 |
| 18-22 | 4 |
| 22-26 | 3 |
| 26-30 | 1 |

Find the ‘mean’ and the ‘mode’ of the above data.
rows.solution:
| Number of days | Number of students \(f_i\) | Class mark \(x_i\) | \(f_i x_i\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2-6 | 11 | 4 | 44 |
| 6-10 | 10 | 8 | 80 |
| 10-14 | 7 | 12 | 84 |
| 14-18 | 4 | 16 | 64 |
| 18-22 | 4 | 20 | 80 |
| 22-26 | 3 | 24 | 72 |
| 26-30 | 1 | 28 | 28 |
| Total | 40 | | 452 |

Mean \(= \dfrac{\sum f_i x_i}{\sum f_i} = \dfrac{452}{40} = 11.3\) days.

The modal class is 2-6 (highest frequency 11). It is the first class, so the frequency of the class before it is 0: \(l = 2\), \(f_1 = 11\), \(f_0 = 0\), \(f_2 = 10\), \(h = 4\):

Mode \(= 2 + \dfrac{11 - 0}{2 \times 11 - 0 - 10} \times 4 = 2 + \dfrac{11}{3} = \dfrac{17}{3} \approx 5.67\) days.

(The marking scheme's table carries the headings "Age (in years)" and "Number of patients" from another set and quotes the answers in years, but its numbers are this data's and are correct.)
